text.p: Following are some of the main
stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified
these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Investors disappointed in ten percent lower Royal Dutch/
Shell Q2 net profits. (p1)
- Amsterdam Stock Exchange closes for the first time above
the 1000 points mark at 1010.97. (p1)
- Publisher Reed-Elsevier's profit growth
in first half of 1997 hit by strong pound. (p1)
- The Amsterdam Options Exchange ranked as the biggest
options exchange in Europe in July. (p1)
- Insurer Central Beheer is considering cancelling the
leave of its technical and computer staff on the weekend of Dec
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Bank Labouchere is seeking an agreement on paying damages
to investors who missed out on recent capital gain in Multihouse
shares. (p2)
- Entertainment group Endemol forms its own
financing company. (p2)
- Many home-owners are changing their mortgages to ones with
lower interest rates, according to the central statistics bureau
CBS. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Banks sound the alarm for mortgage fraud with counterfeit
documents. (p9)
- Carbon producer Norit sees first half net soar
66 pct from Dfl 8.3 mln to Dfl 13.8 mln. (p23)
- Merchant bank Kempen & Co's first half net jumps 129
pct to Dfl 23.9 mln from Dfl 12.4 mln. (p23)
TROUW
- Airlines' opposition against Amsterdam Schiphol Airport's
measures against noisy aircraft increases. (p1)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Strong dollar will boost Dutch competitiveness, but will
lead to a slightly higher inflation next year, according to
central planning bureau CPB. (p1)
--Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
